project.name: GuWorld
project.description: A text-based RPG web game inspired by Reverend Insanity (Cổ Chân Nhân), combining macro resource management, survival, deck-building, and turn-based combat where all abilities come from equipped Gu insects rather than innate character talent. The stack pairs a Go (Gin) backend for concurrent game logic and combat with a Next.js (React) frontend using Tailwind CSS and Zustand, backed by PostgreSQL and Redis.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with PROJECT.md to learn what GuWorld is: a Reverend Insanity-inspired text RPG where the player is only an energy vessel (Aperture) and all power comes from Gu insects. The document outlines the core loop—explore, gather stones and materials, feed Gu, refine, then fight—and the Gin + Next.js + PostgreSQL/Redis stack that implements it.

tour.title: Core Gameplay Spec
tour.description: GameplayCore_DesignSpec.md turns the high-level loop into concrete rules: player creation, refining tick formulas, mastery curves, Gu class behaviors, and CanActivateGu validation. Read this after the overview so you know which backend handlers and frontend screens must honor the same invariants.

tour.title: Backend Bootstrap
tour.description: main.go is the runtime entry point: it loads environment config, opens PostgreSQL, seeds schemas and content registries, starts the hunger background worker, and launches the Gin HTTP server. Every API request and worker tick ultimately traces back to the wiring performed here.
tour.languageLesson: Go programs start at package main’s func main(). Here, side-effectful bootstrap (DB, seeds, workers) runs before Listen, which is a common pattern for long-lived API servers.

tour.title: API Router & Auth
tour.description: server.go registers the full game API surface—cultivation, combat, exploration, shops, marketplace, and more—while auth middleware attaches the authenticated player ID from JWT cookies or headers. Together they define how HTTP paths map to handler packages you will explore next.
tour.languageLesson: Gin groups routes under middleware stacks: public auth endpoints stay outside JWT protection, while gameplay routes run after AuthMiddleware populates the request context.

tour.title: Domain Models
tour.description: The models package is the shared vocabulary of the backend. player.go holds Player, GuInstance, and CombatState; gu.go and item.go define dictionary types and JSONB scanning; monster.go bridges templates to combatants. These structs are the highest fan-in code in the graph—almost every handler imports them.

tour.title: Database & Content Seeds
tour.description: db.go connects to PostgreSQL, applies schema, and seeds dictionaries from CSV and hardcoded data. The Gu.csv, Item.csv, and Recipe.csv schemas are the authoritative content sources loaded into registries that models and handlers reference at runtime—linking design spreadsheets to live game data.
tour.languageLesson: CSV dictionaries are seeded once at startup into PostgreSQL and in-memory registries, so gameplay code reads stable IDs without parsing spreadsheets on every request.

tour.title: Player Lifecycle API
tour.description: player.go implements the central player HTTP API: registration and login, stat snapshots, exploration state, Gu inventory mutations, item use, and recharge flows. This handler is the main bridge between session identity (from Step 4’s auth) and the Player types from Step 5.

tour.title: Exploration & Combat
tour.description: exploration.go drives the grid world—cell generation, movement, encounters, and rewards—while combat.go initializes fights, processes attacks, enemy AI, loot, and Gu effect hooks. These two handlers embody the explore → fight half of the core loop described in Steps 1–2.

tour.title: Refine & Gu Effects
tour.description: refine.go exposes recipe listing and RNG refinement with material costs, completing the feed-and-craft progression. gu_effects.go validates usable Gu, builds combat actions, and ticks status effects—connecting dictionary definitions to moment-to-moment battle behavior.

tour.title: Frontend Game Store
tour.description: useGameStore.ts is the Zustand hub with the highest fan-in on the frontend: it holds player, combat, and dictionary state and performs cookie-authenticated REST calls to the Go API. Nearly every UI component reads actions and selectors from here instead of calling fetch directly.
tour.languageLesson: Zustand stores are plain objects with actions; components subscribe to slices of state, which keeps the Next.js UI in sync with backend responses without prop-drilling through page.tsx.

tour.title: App Shell & Key UI
tour.description: page.tsx bootstraps the session, polls player status, and switches between cultivation, exploration, shop, arena, and chat views. ExplorationMap, CombatScreen, GuInventory, and Aperture are the primary surfaces for the loop you traced on the server—each delegates to the game store from Step 10.
